feature: Configuration from env: CS_ENDPOINT (required, http(s), trailing slash trimmed), CS_TENANT (required), CS_SERVICE (default: DeriveService(POD_NAME or hostname): strips Deployment '<hash>-<5>', ReplicaSet/DaemonSet '-<5>', StatefulSet '-<n>' suffixes; required when underivable), CS_CLIENT_ID (default = service), CS_PUBLISHER (default health-sidecar; undocumented in README), CS_PROBE auto|actuator|http|tcp, CS_PORT (0..65535; required for non-auto), CS_PATH (leading / added), CS_SCHEME http|https, CS_HOST list (127.0.0.1,::1), CS_IGNORE_PORTS ranges (15000-15099), CS_INTERVAL 15s (≥1s), CS_HEARTBEAT 30s (raised to ≥ interval), CS_PROBE_TIMEOUT 3s, CS_REPORT_TIMEOUT 5s, CS_STARTUP_GRACE 5m, CS_RETRY_DELAY 2s, CS_LISTEN :9465, CS_CA_FILE, CS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY, instance from CS_INSTANCE_ID/POD_NAME, POD_NAMESPACE, NODE_NAME, CS_CLUSTER, CS_VERSION; all errors joined and reported at once; exit code 2 on invalid config
how_to_verify: Run with no env → exit 2 listing both required vars; with each bad value → named error; DeriveService table. Existing: TestFromEnvDefaults, TestFromEnvOverridesAndValidation, TestDeriveService, TestParsePortRanges

feature: Port discovery: parses /proc/net/tcp and /proc/net/tcp6 (either may be missing), keeps LISTEN (0A) sockets only, hex port decode, dedup + ascending, skips the sidecar's own listen port and CS_IGNORE_PORTS; works in a pod because containers share one network namespace and need no RBAC
how_to_verify: Run the binary next to a listener on 18080 → /status.target names 18080; with CS_IGNORE_PORTS=18080 → stays UNKNOWN 'no health target'. Existing: TestParseKeepsOnlyListeningSockets, TestListeningPortsMergesTablesAndSkips

feature: Probe ladder (CS_PROBE=auto): pass 1 GET /actuator/health on every port (lowest first) accepting any health document; pass 2 /health,/healthz,/readyz,/ready,/livez,/q/health accepting a document or UP; pass 3 '/' accepting UP or DOWN (any answer <500 is UP, 5xx is DOWN); then TCP connect to the lowest port; hosts tried in order (127.0.0.1 then ::1); http first then https when the port speaks TLS (Go 'HTTPS server' hint); redirects are answers, not followed; first target kept
how_to_verify: Stubs: 9001 plain 404 on everything, 9002 /healthz 200, 9003 /actuator/health doc → target 9003 actuator; remove 9003 → 9002 http; only a raw TCP listener → tcp mode. Existing: TestDetectPrefersActuatorOverAnyPort, TestDetectFallsBackToRootThenTCP, TestDetectSwitchesToHTTPS

feature: Status normalisation and classification: UP/OK/PASS/HEALTHY/GREEN/SERVING → UP; DOWN/FAIL/FAILED/ERROR/UNHEALTHY/OUT_OF_SERVICE/FATAL/RED/NOT_SERVING → DOWN; ''/UNKNOWN → UNKNOWN (then HTTP code decides); other words passed through upper-cased (service treats as DEGRADED); without a document: 5xx DOWN, <400 UP, 4xx on a health path UNKNOWN (with 'check CS_PATH' message), 4xx on '/' UP; components from `components` or legacy status-bearing `details`; body limit 64 KiB
how_to_verify: Stub returning {status:'WARN'} → report status WARN → backend monitor lastStatus DEGRADED. Existing: TestNormalize, TestProbePlainHTTPClassification, TestProbeDownDocumentAndOldActuatorShape, TestProbeActuatorDocument

feature: Pinned target (CS_PORT set): CS_PROBE=auto + path → http; auto without path → actuator path; tcp ignores path; actuator/http default their paths; scheme defaults to http; discovery and rediscovery disabled
how_to_verify: Run with CS_PORT=18080 CS_PATH=/ping → /status.target http://127.0.0.1:18080/ping; CS_PROBE=tcp CS_PORT=18080 → tcp://…

feature: Startup rule: until the app has answered UP once and while the grace (CS_STARTUP_GRACE) runs, the report is UNKNOWN ('starting: waiting for the app to listen' / '…first healthy answer from <target>'); no target after the grace → UNKNOWN with 'set CS_PORT and CS_PATH'; a pinned target that never answered UP stays UNKNOWN after the grace with a config hint; once UP was seen, real statuses flow (DOWN after the app dies)
e2e_path: CLI (fake clock in tests; real run with CS_STARTUP_GRACE=10s)
how_to_verify: Start sidecar before the app → first reports UNKNOWN (backend ignores: no notice); start app → UP; kill app → DOWN. Existing: TestStartupGraceReportsUnknownUntilFirstUp, TestNoListeningPortStaysUnknown, TestPinnedTargetThatNeverAnswersUpStaysUnknown

feature: Flap damping: a non-UP probe is repeated after CS_RETRY_DELAY (2s) before it counts; the second answer wins
how_to_verify: Stub that fails exactly one request then recovers → report stays UP; set CS_RETRY_DELAY=0 → DOWN reported. Covered indirectly by agent tests (RetryDelay=0 in harness; verify there is a case with a delay)

feature: Send policy: a report is posted when the signature (status + non-UP components) changes or CS_HEARTBEAT elapsed since the last successful send; every tick is jittered by up to 20% of CS_INTERVAL; on transport/5xx failure exponential backoff 1s→60s (+20% jitter) keeping only the latest report (dirty flag); a 4xx other than 408/409/429 is permanent: logged as 'report rejected', not retried until the next change/heartbeat; nothing retried mid-shutdown
how_to_verify: Stub 500 → /status.sendError set, retries at 1,2,4,8…s; stub 400 → one error log, next send at heartbeat; stub 409 → retried like 5xx. Existing: TestReportsChangesAndHeartbeats, TestSendFailuresBackOffAndKeepLatest, TestSendClassifiesFailures

feature: Report wire contract (sidecar → POST /v1/health/reports): {tenantId, service, status, components?, message?, observedAt (UTC ms), publisher, instance{id, namespace?, node?, cluster?, version?, sidecar (binary version), leaving?}} with headers Content-Type/Accept application/json, X-Client-Id = CS_CLIENT_ID, User-Agent health-sidecar/<version>; matches HealthReportCommand/ReportInstance (id ≤253, namespace/node ≤253, cluster/version/sidecar ≤100)
how_to_verify: Run sidecar against the backend; GET /v1/health/monitors/{id}/instances shows the pod with sidecar version; a 253-char pod id accepted, 254 → 400 (permanent, logged). Existing: TestSendPostsReportWithClientId, reportBindsActuatorShapedComponentsAndReturns202

feature: Graceful shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT cancels the loop, one final report is sent with instance.leaving=true and message 'instance shutting down' within CS_REPORT_TIMEOUT (skipped if nothing was ever composed), then the status server shuts down within 2s and the process exits 0; no preStop hook or terminationGracePeriodSeconds is set in the snippets (defaults: 30s)
how_to_verify: Run against the backend, kill -TERM, check log 'leaving report sent', GET instances shows left=true, exit code 0, elapsed < 3s. Existing: TestRunSendsLeavingReportOnShutdown

feature: Rediscovery: when an unpinned target becomes unreachable and its port is no longer listening, the target is dropped and discovery runs again next tick (the app restarted on another port)
how_to_verify: Discover on 18080, stop it, start the app on 18081 → /status.target switches within two intervals. Existing: TestRediscoversWhenPortDisappears

feature: Sidecar's own endpoints on CS_LISTEN (:9465): GET /healthz → 200 'ok' text/plain (liveness); GET /status → JSON {version, service, tenant, instance, target?, upSeen, lastReport?, lastSendAt?, sendError?, reportsSent}; other methods/paths 404/405; ReadHeaderTimeout 5s
how_to_verify: curl both; confirm /status reflects a failed send. Existing: TestHandler

feature: TLS to the endpoint: TLS ≥1.2; CS_CA_FILE PEM appended to the system pool (startup error if unreadable or holds no certs); CS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY opt-in; HTTP(S)_PROXY honoured from env for reports (never for localhost probes); localhost probes skip certificate verification by design
how_to_verify: Stub https backend with a private CA: no CA file → send error 'x509'; CS_CA_FILE → ok; bad file → exit 2. Existing: TestNewClientRejectsBadCAFile

feature: Container image: multi-stage build registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/go-toolset:1.24 → ubi9/ubi-micro:9.5, CGO disabled, -trimpath, -s -w, VERSION build arg → main.version, UBI CA bundle copied to /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt, USER 1001 (numeric, so runAsNonRoot validates), EXPOSE 9465, ENTRYPOINT the binary; .dockerignore excludes deploy/, README, tests; README claims ~10 MB

feature: Runs under restricted-v2 / non-root: binary needs no writable filesystem, no capabilities, no privilege escalation, works with an arbitrary UID (no /etc/passwd entry, HOME unset) and readOnlyRootFilesystem; reads only /proc/net/tcp* of its own netns
e2e_path: CLI (docker run with the flags) or pod
how_to_verify: Run the image as uid 1000660000 with --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, seccomp default, and an app in the same network namespace (--network container:app) → reports UP; strace/`ls -la /proc/1/fd` shows no writes

feature: Kustomize component: `components: [<component>]` appends the health-sidecar container to every Deployment and StatefulSet (regex target) with envFrom ConfigMap cs-health-sidecar (CS_ENDPOINT, CS_TENANT, CS_CLUSTER), Downward API POD_NAME/POD_NAMESPACE/NODE_NAME, CS_SERVICE and CS_VERSION from app.kubernetes.io/name|version labels, port cs-status 9465, liveness /healthz every 30s, requests 10m/16Mi, limits 50m/32Mi, securityContext {allowPrivilegeEscalation:false, readOnlyRootFilesystem:true, runAsNonRoot:true, drop ALL, seccomp RuntimeDefault}; example overlay generates the ConfigMap without a hash suffix

feature: Probes and resources in the snippets: liveness httpGet /healthz on cs-status every 30s (no failureThreshold/timeouts set → defaults 3/1s); NO readiness probe (sidecar counts as ready immediately; the app's readiness governs the pod) and NO startup probe; requests 10m/16Mi, limits 50m/32Mi; no terminationGracePeriodSeconds/preStop (relies on the 2s+timeout internal shutdown and the pod default 30s)
how_to_verify: Run the image for 10 min against a stub and record RSS/CPU vs the 32Mi/50m limits; review whether the missing readiness/startup probes matter for the native-sidecar start ordering

feature: Startup ordering & restart behaviour: regular sidecar may start before/after the app and reports UNKNOWN until the app answers UP (no false outage during rolling deploys); native form starts first and is stopped after the app; app restart → DOWN (after retry delay) or rediscovery if the port changed; sidecar crash → liveness restart, the app is unaffected (no shared volume/socket, only the pod network namespace); backend unreachable → backoff, app unaffected; silence longer than 90s (sidecar and app both dead, or network cut) → backend declares the service DOWN naming the pod
where: agent.go:147-235; HealthSweepUseCase.java:284-307; README.md (sidecar) 'What it reports and when'
e2e_path: docker (two containers sharing a netns) + backend; cannot be done in a real pod here
how_to_verify: Script: start sidecar, then app → UNKNOWN→UP; kill app → DOWN notice after 2 reports; restart app → recovered; kill sidecar → (simulated liveness) restart → UP, no new notice; stop backend → sidecar backoff logs, resume → next heartbeat accepted

feature: Logging & observability: sidecar logs JSON (slog) with version/service/tenant/instance/endpoint at start, 'health target found', 'reported' on change, 'report failed; will retry' with backoff, 'report rejected' on 4xx, 'leaving report sent'; backend logs client id at debug, rejected calls at info, sweep transitions at info, notice opens/retires at info, staleness pause at warn; no secrets logged
e2e_path: CLI (read logs during the E2E runs)
how_to_verify: Capture both logs during F-91 and check each line exists and is parseable

feature: E2E human flow: publish an outage in the UI (with ticket and services) → it appears live in a second browser tab's feed without refresh and in `GET /v1/feed` for a consumer with the service filter → resolve from the UI → gone from both, permalink RETIRED with the note in history
how_to_verify: Playwright script with two pages + curl assertions; evidence: screenshots and the stream log

feature: E2E sidecar flow: app container + sidecar (shared netns) + backend + UI; app UP → monitor auto-registered with instance; app DOWN → after failureThreshold reports an OUTAGE '<service> is down' appears in the UI feed (type Outage) and `/v1/health/monitors/{id}/instances` names the pod; app UP → notice retired; sidecar SIGTERM → instance left=true; second pod keeps the service UP while one pod is DOWN (rollup '1 of 2 pods UP' → UP by default)
how_to_verify: Scripted run with timestamps; evidence: backend log, sidecar /status, feed JSON, UI screenshot

feature: E2E failure paths: backend down (UI error state + Try again; sidecar backoff and recovery), sidecar/app silent beyond the window (DOWN notice naming pods), slow backend (sidecar CS_REPORT_TIMEOUT fires, retries), bad input (400 text surfaced in UI; sidecar 400 logged as permanent), missing/invalid client id (401/400), expired/unknown Last-Event-ID (snapshot fallback), Mongo down (backend 5xx {error} / SSE keepalive continues; recovery without restart)
how_to_verify: Scripted fault injection with the compose-style environment; record each observed behaviour against the expected one
